# AK(3) Minimum-Tail Fox Coset Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use
> superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps
> use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Reduce the full Fox equation for the repositioned minimum tail
and seek a rigorous finite quotient obstruction.

**Architecture:** Isolate the right ideal generated by two bridge
variables, identify its subgroup \(P\), prove the Bass--Serre geometry of
\(P\), and project the remaining cyclic-module equation to finite coset
modules.

**Tech Stack:** Markdown proof, pure Python, amalgam normal form,
Bass--Serre axes, integral permutation modules, `runpy`.

## Global Constraints

- Scalar augmentation is not the full Fox equation.
- A finite quotient which leaves any target residue is not a nonlift
  certificate.
- Bounded scans are evidence only; symbolic coefficient reductions are
  the theorem.
- No AC graph search.
- AK(3) remains open.

---

### Task 1: Reduce the Fox coefficients

- [x] Expand \(\Xi=A_0+A_Uu+A_Vv+A_Ww\).
- [x] Prove \(A_VR+A_WR=I_P\).
- [x] Reduce solvability to one equation in
  \(\mathbb Z[P\backslash G]\).

### Task 2: Determine \(P\)

- [x] Prove the projected axes are disjoint at distance one.
- [x] Apply tree ping-pong to prove \(P\cong F_2\).
- [x] Prove \(P\cap\langle c\rangle=1\).
- [x] Prove \(P\) has infinite index.

### Task 3: Apply a finite Fox quotient

- [x] Map \(G\) onto \(S_4\) and \(P\) onto a point stabilizer.
- [x] Replay the exact four-coset coefficient vectors.
- [x] Prove only target residues in the point stabilizer survive.
- [x] State explicitly that the identity target survives.
- [x] Run full replay, diff audit, and hostile review.
- [x] Commit and push the verified checkpoint.
